name: Leeward Design System
setup: Set data-theme="light" | "dark" | "auto" on a root element.

components.name: Accordion
components.purpose: Expandable sections for fees, FAQs and account details.

props.name: type
props.description: single opens one item at a time, multiple lets people open several.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of each trigger, to fit the page outline.

do: Write the trigger as a question or a clear topic.
Set headingLevel so triggers fit the page outline.
dont: Do not hide information people need to make a decision, such as the fee of a transfer.
accessibility: Triggers are buttons inside headings with aria-expanded.
Arrow keys move between triggers. Behavior from Radix Accordion.
components.example: <Accordion items={[{ value: "fees", title: "What does a transfer cost?", content: "Free between Leeward accounts." }]} />

components.name: Alert
components.purpose: Inline message on the page: what happened and what to do next.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons or links under the message.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Shows a close button. The parent decides what closing means.

props.name: live
props.description: Use "alert" only for urgent problems that need attention now. Default "status".

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Use info for useful context, success after something completed, warning before a limit, danger when something failed.
Lead with what happened in the title, then what to do in the text.
Use live="alert" only for urgent failures.
dont: Do not use an Alert for field errors: put the error on the field.
Do not stack more than one Alert at the top of a screen.
accessibility: role="status" by default, role="alert" when urgent.
Every tone has an icon and text, never color alone.
The dismiss button is labelled.
components.example: <Alert tone="warning" title="You are close to your daily limit">₺1.500 left today.</Alert>

components.name: Avatar
components.purpose: Initials, image or category icon for a person or merchant.

props.name: name
props.description: Person or merchant name. Used for initials and as the accessible name.

props.name: icon
props.description: One of the names in `icons` at the top of this manifest.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Set when a visible name sits next to the avatar, so screen readers do not hear it twice.

do: Set `decorative` when the name is visible next to it.
dont: Do not use an avatar as the only way to identify a person.
accessibility: `role="img"` named by `name`, or hidden when decorative.
Falls back to initials if the image fails.
components.example: <Avatar name="Deniz Yılmaz" decorative />

components.name: Badge
components.purpose: Short status label such as Pending, Paid or Declined.

props.name: icon
props.description: Status badges show an icon by default so state never depends on color. Pass null to hide it.

props.name: appearance
props.description: subtle for lists and tables, solid for counts and strong status.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Keep it to one or two words.
Status tones add an icon by default.
Use appearance="solid" for strong status and counts, subtle for lists.
dont: Do not use as a button.
Do not remove the icon on status tones without another non-color signal.
accessibility: Text is part of the content, so screen readers read it.
Every tone passes AA against its background.
components.example: <Badge tone="warning">Pending</Badge>

components.name: Button
components.purpose: Triggers an action. One primary button per screen or section.

props.name: variant
props.description: primary: the one main action on a screen. secondary and outline: alternatives. danger: irreversible actions only.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner, keeps the label for screen readers and blocks repeat clicks.

props.name: iconStart
props.description: One of the names in `icons` at the top of this manifest.

props.name: iconEnd
props.description: One of the names in `icons` at the top of this manifest.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Use primary for the one main action, secondary or outline for alternatives, ghost for low emphasis, danger only for irreversible actions.
Sizes: xs 32, sm 36, md 44 (default), lg 48, xl 56 px. Use xl full width for the last step of a mobile flow.
Write the label as the outcome: "Send ₺250", "Freeze card".
Use `loading` while the action runs, so the label stays readable and repeat clicks are blocked.
Every size keeps a 44 px hit area on touch screens.
dont: Do not use danger for normal payments. Sending money is not an error.
Do not put two primary buttons next to each other.
Do not use a Button for navigation to another page: use a link.
Do not disable a submit button to hide errors. Let people submit and show the error.
accessibility: Native `<button>` with `type="button"` by default.
Loading uses `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, keeps focus and keeps the accessible name.
Small size keeps a 44px hit area with an invisible extension.
Focus ring is 2px with a 2px offset, 3:1 against every surface.
components.example: <Button variant="primary" iconStart="arrow-up-right" onClick={send}>Send money</Button>

components.name: Card
components.purpose: Surface that groups related content.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Use `elevated` for primary objects like accounts, `outlined` for lists, `filled` for quiet grouping.
Pick `as` for meaning: `section` with a heading, `article` for self-contained items.
dont: Do not nest elevated cards.
Do not make a whole card clickable if it contains other buttons.
accessibility: No interactive behavior of its own.
components.example: <Card variant="elevated" padding="lg">...</Card>

components.name: Checkbox
components.purpose: A yes or no choice inside a form, or one of many independent choices.
do: Write the label as a statement people agree with: "Save this person as a recipient".
dont: Do not use for settings that apply immediately. Use Switch.
Do not pre-check consent boxes.
accessibility: Built on Radix Checkbox with a native-like label.
20px box with a 44px hit area. Supports indeterminate.
components.example: <Checkbox label="Save this person as a recipient" onCheckedChange={setSave} />

components.name: Chip
components.purpose: Filter toggle, for example in a transaction list.

props.name: selected
props.description: Filter chips toggle. The state is exposed with aria-pressed and shown with a check mark.

props.name: icon
props.description: One of the names in `icons` at the top of this manifest.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Group chips in an element with `role="group"` and an `aria-label`.
dont: Do not use chips as navigation tabs. Use Tabs.
Do not use for actions that move money.
accessibility: Toggle button with `aria-pressed`. Selected chips show a check mark, not only color.
components.example: <Chip selected={selected} onSelectedChange={setSelected}>Money in</Chip>

components.name: Dialog
components.purpose: Modal for a decision that needs full attention, such as confirming a transfer or freezing a card.

props.name: title
props.description: Required. Read when the dialog opens.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Element that opens the dialog, usually a Button.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons for the footer. Put the main action last.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Label for the close button. Defaults to "Close".

props.name: hideClose
props.description: Hide the close button for flows that must end with an explicit choice.

do: Write `title` as a question: "Freeze your card?".
Put the main action last in `actions`. Use danger only if it cannot be undone.
dont: Do not open a dialog on page load.
Do not use for information that could sit on the page.
accessibility: Traps focus, closes on Escape, returns focus to the trigger.
Named by `title` and described by `description`.
components.example: <Dialog title="Freeze your card?" trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Freeze card</Button>} actions={<Button>Freeze card</Button>} />

components.name: Divider
components.purpose: Separates groups of content.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional text in the middle, for example "or".

props.name: decorative
props.description: Decorative dividers are hidden from screen readers. Set false when it separates real sections.

do: Prefer spacing to dividers. Use a divider when two groups would otherwise blur together.
dont: Do not use a divider as the only signal that sections differ.
accessibility: Hidden from screen readers by default. Set decorative={false} when it separates real sections.
components.example: <Divider label="or" />

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.purpose: Secondary actions for an item, behind a More button.

props.name: trigger
props.description: A single focusable trigger, usually an IconButton labelled "More actions".

do: Order actions by how often they are used. Destructive actions go last and are separated.
dont: Do not hide the main action in a menu.
Do not use a menu for navigation.
accessibility: menu role with menuitems. Arrow keys move, Enter selects, Escape closes. Behavior from Radix.
components.example: <DropdownMenu trigger={<IconButton icon="more-vertical" label="More actions" />} actions={[{ label: "Copy IBAN", icon: "copy", onSelect: copy }]} />

components.name: EmptyState
components.purpose: Shown when a list or search has nothing to show yet.

props.name: icon
props.description: One of the names in `icons` at the top of this manifest.

props.name: title
props.description: Say what is missing in plain words: "No payments yet".

props.name: description
props.description: Say what people can do next.

do: Say what is missing, then what people can do.
Offer one action when there is a clear next step.
dont: Do not blame people for an empty state.
accessibility: Real heading at the level you choose. The illustration is decorative.
components.example: <EmptyState icon="wallet-money" title="No payments yet" description="Your payments show up here." />

components.name: Heading
components.purpose: Section and page headings with a required outline level.

props.name: level
props.description: Document outline level. Required so the page structure is always intentional.

props.name: size
props.description: Visual size. Defaults to the heading role of the same level. Display and title sizes are fluid.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Set `level` for the document outline and `size` for the look. They can differ.
One `level={1}` per screen.
dont: Do not skip levels, for example h1 to h3.
Do not use Heading only to make text big. Use Text or AmountDisplay.
accessibility: `level` is required so the outline is intentional.
Large headings use `text-wrap: balance`.
components.example: <Heading level={2} size="sm">Recent activity</Heading>

components.name: Icon
components.purpose: Solar icons (480 Design, CC BY 4.0) on a 24 px grid: 142 icons in three weights. Use linear by default, bold for selected or active states, duotone for illustrations and empty states.

props.name: name
props.description: One of the names in `icons` at the top of this manifest.

props.name: weight
props.description: linear for most UI, bold for selected or active states, duotone for illustrations and empty states.

props.name: label
props.description: Give a label only when the icon carries meaning on its own. Without one the icon is hidden from assistive tech.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Pair icons with text for anything important.
Give `label` only when the icon carries meaning on its own.
dont: Do not draw new SVGs inline in product code. Add them with `pnpm icons:import` (see scripts/import-solar-icons.ts).
Do not use an icon as the only signal of state.
accessibility: Decorative by default (`aria-hidden`).
With `label` it becomes `role="img"` with that name.
Uses `currentColor`, so it follows the text tone.
components.example: <Icon name="lock" label="Secured" />

components.name: IconButton
components.purpose: Icon-only button for secondary actions such as close, settings or show balance.

props.name: icon
props.description: One of the names in `icons` at the top of this manifest.

props.name: label
props.description: Required. Becomes the accessible name. Describe the outcome: "Close", "Show balance".

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Give `label` the outcome: "Close", "Show balance".
Wrap in Tooltip when the icon is not obvious.
dont: Do not use for moving money. Send, pay and transfer always need a text Button.
Do not use an icon without a label.
accessibility: `label` is required and becomes `aria-label`.
44 by 44px target at md size, extended hit area at sm.
Use `aria-pressed` for toggles such as hide balance.
components.example: <IconButton icon="close" label="Close" onClick={onClose} />

components.name: Link
components.purpose: Navigation to another page or site.

props.name: external
props.description: Opens in a new tab with an icon and screen reader text that say so.

props.name: variant
props.description: standalone for links on their own line, inline for links inside a sentence (always underlined).

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Use inline links inside sentences: they are always underlined.
Use external for other sites, so people know a new tab opens.
dont: Do not use a link for actions such as Send or Delete: use Button.
Do not write "click here". Name the destination.
accessibility: Native anchor. External links add an icon and screen reader text.
components.example: <Link href="/fees" variant="standalone">See all fees</Link>

components.name: ListItem
components.purpose: Row in a list with title, description, leading and trailing slots. Use inside List.

props.name: leading
props.description: Avatar or icon on the start side.

props.name: trailing
props.description: Value, badge or control on the end side.

props.name: href
props.description: Makes the whole row a link.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Makes the whole row a button.

props.name: chevron
props.description: Show a chevron when the row opens another screen.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Overrides the accessible name of the interactive row.

do: Use `href` for navigation and `onClick` for actions. The whole row becomes the target.
Add `chevron` when the row opens another screen.
dont: Do not put a button inside an interactive row.
Do not use for transactions. Use TransactionRow.
accessibility: Renders `li` inside `ul`. Rows are at least 44px tall.
Interactive rows use a native link or button.
components.example: <List><ListItem title="Security" description="Passcode, Face ID" href="/security" chevron /></List>

components.name: ProgressBar
components.purpose: Progress toward a goal or limit.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label, for example "Monthly spending limit".

props.name: valueText
props.description: Text shown on the end side, for example "₺7.500 of ₺10.000". Defaults to a percentage.

props.name: tone
props.description: Pair warning and danger with words in valueText, for example "90% used". Color is never the only signal.

do: Always set `valueText` in words for money: "₺4.500 of ₺10.000".
Use warning and danger with words: "92% used, ₺800 left".
dont: Do not use for loading. Use Skeleton or a loading Button.
accessibility: `progressbar` role named by the label, with `aria-valuetext`.
components.example: <ProgressBar label="Holiday fund" value={4500} max={10000} valueText="₺4.500 of ₺10.000" />

components.name: RadioGroup
components.purpose: Pick exactly one option from 2 to 5 visible choices.

props.name: label
props.description: Group label, read as the question.

do: Write `label` as the question: "When should it arrive?".
Add `description` to explain the consequence of each option.
dont: Do not use for more than about 5 options.
Do not leave a group with no default unless the choice must be explicit.
accessibility: `radiogroup` role named by the label. Arrow keys move between options.
Descriptions are linked with `aria-describedby`.
components.example: <RadioGroup label="When should it arrive?" options={options} defaultValue="now" />

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.purpose: Pick one view or filter from 2 to 5 short options.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the group, for example "Period".

do: Keep labels to one word when you can: Week, Month, Year.
Use fullWidth on phones.
dont: Do not use it for navigation between pages: use Tabs.
Do not use it for form choices that need a submit: use RadioGroup.
accessibility: radiogroup role named by label. Arrow keys move. One option is always selected.
The selected option uses a raised surface and shadow, not color alone.
components.example: <SegmentedControl label="Period" options={[{ value: "week", label: "Week" }, { value: "month", label: "Month" }]} />

components.name: Select
components.purpose: Pick one option from a short list. Built on Radix Select.

props.name: size
props.description: sm 36 px, md 44 px (default), lg 48 px.

do: Use for 5 to 15 options. Use RadioGroup for fewer, a searchable list for more.
Write a placeholder that asks: "Choose an account".
dont: Do not use Select for actions.
Do not hide important differences between options. Use RadioGroup with descriptions.
accessibility: Trigger is a labelled combobox. Full keyboard support from Radix.
Options are 44px tall.
components.example: <Select label="Pay from" options={[{ value: "everyday", label: "Everyday account" }]} onValueChange={setAccount} />

components.name: Sheet
components.purpose: Panel for a task in context, such as filters or transaction details.

props.name: side
props.description: bottom on phones by default; end slides in from the right on wider screens.

do: Use side="bottom" on phones and side="end" for side panels on wide screens.
Put the main action last in footer.
dont: Do not open a sheet from inside another sheet.
accessibility: Modal dialog: traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus. Named by title.
components.example: <Sheet title="Filter transactions" trigger={<Button variant="outline">Filter</Button>}>...</Sheet>

components.name: Skeleton
components.purpose: Placeholder while content loads.

props.name: width
props.description: Any CSS length. Defaults to 100% for text and rect.

props.name: height
props.description: Any CSS length. Text skeletons follow the line height.

props.name: lines
props.description: Number of text lines. The last one is shorter.

do: Match the shape of the content that will appear.
Mark the loading region with `role="status"` and `aria-busy`.
dont: Do not show skeletons for more than a few seconds without a message.
accessibility: Hidden from screen readers. No shimmer with reduced motion.

components.name: Spinner
components.purpose: Short wait indicator when the shape of the result is unknown.

props.name: label
props.description: With a label the spinner is announced as a status. Without one it is decorative.

do: Give it a label when it is the only thing on screen.
dont: Do not use for page content: use Skeleton.
Do not use inside buttons: use Button loading.
accessibility: With a label it is a status region. It keeps turning slowly under reduced motion so it never looks frozen.
components.example: <Spinner label="Loading your accounts" />

components.name: Stepper
components.purpose: Shows where people are in a multi-step flow.

props.name: steps
props.description: Short step names, for example ["Recipient", "Amount", "Review", "Confirm"].

props.name: current
props.description: Zero-based index of the current step.

props.name: variant
props.description: compact shows "Step 2 of 4" and a bar, for phones.

do: Use short step names.
Use variant="compact" on phones.
dont: Do not use for more than 5 steps.
Do not make steps clickable unless going back is safe.
accessibility: nav landmark with an ordered list. The current step has aria-current="step", completed steps say so in text.
components.example: <Stepper steps={["Recipient", "Amount", "Review", "Confirm"]} current={1} />

components.name: Switch
components.purpose: A setting that applies immediately, such as online card payments.

props.name: label
props.description: Describe the setting, not the state: "Card payments online", not "On".

do: Label the setting, not the state: "Online card payments".
dont: Do not use inside a form that has a submit button. Use Checkbox.
Do not write "On" or "Off" as the label.
accessibility: `switch` role from Radix. Track meets 3:1 against every surface.
44px wide target.
components.example: <Switch label="Online card payments" checked={on} onCheckedChange={setOn} />

components.name: Tabs
components.purpose: Switch between views of the same object, such as Activity and Statements.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the tab list, for example "Account views".

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretch tabs to fill the width, for mobile segmented views.

do: Give `label` a name for the tab list.
Keep labels to one or two words.
dont: Do not use tabs for steps in a flow.
Do not hide required form fields in other tabs.
accessibility: Radix Tabs: arrow keys move between tabs, Tab moves into the panel.
Active tab uses weight and an underline, not only color.
components.example: <Tabs label="Account views" items={[{ value: "activity", label: "Activity", content: <Activity /> }]} />

components.name: Text
components.purpose: Body, label and caption text with token-based type roles and tones.

props.name: tone
props.description: primary = default text, secondary = muted, tertiary = subtle. All pass AA on every surface.

props.name: tabular
props.description: Tabular figures, for numbers that line up in columns.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Cut to one line with an ellipsis.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Use `tabular` for numbers that line up in columns.
Use tone `secondary` for supporting text and `tertiary` only for hints and captions.
dont: Do not use tone `success` or `danger` as the only signal of state. Add an icon or words.
Do not style text with raw font sizes.
accessibility: Every tone passes WCAG 2.2 AA on every surface in light and dark themes.
Pick `as` for meaning: `p` for paragraphs, `span` inline, `label` with `htmlFor`.
components.example: <Text variant="body-sm" tone="secondary">Transfers to other banks take up to one working day.</Text>

components.name: TextField
components.purpose: Single-line input with label, hint, error, prefix and suffix.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Required: placeholders are not labels.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid and links the message to the input.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Short text or symbol before the value, for example "₺".

props.name: numeric
props.description: Use tabular figures, for amounts and codes.

props.name: size
props.description: sm 36 px, md 44 px (default, touch friendly), lg 48 px.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Always set a visible `label`.
Sizes: sm 36, md 44 (default), lg 48 px. On touch screens small fields still get 44 px and 16 px text so iOS does not zoom.
Use `hint` for format help before people type, `error` for what went wrong and how to fix it.
For amounts use `prefix="₺"`, `inputMode="decimal"` and `numeric`.
dont: Do not use the placeholder as a label.
Do not write errors that blame: "Invalid input". Say what to do: "This IBAN is too short. Check it and try again."
accessibility: Label is linked with `htmlFor`.
Hint and error are linked with `aria-describedby`. Error sets `aria-invalid`.
Errors pair an icon with text and a thicker border, never color alone.
components.example: <TextField label="IBAN" hint="26 characters, starts with TR" error={error} />

components.name: Textarea
components.purpose: Multi-line text for payment notes and messages.

props.name: showCount
props.description: Shows "12 of 140" and announces it politely as people type.

props.name: ...rest
props.description: Other native props are passed to the root element.

do: Show the limit with maxLength and showCount when there is one.
dont: Do not use it for single-line values such as names or IBANs: use TextField.
accessibility: Visible label, hint and error linked like TextField.
The counter is announced politely.
components.example: <Textarea label="Payment note" maxLength={140} showCount optional />

components.name: Toast
components.purpose: Short confirmation after an action, such as "Money sent". Use with ToastProvider and useToast.
do: Confirm what happened in plain words.
Errors stay until dismissed. Other tones hide after 6 seconds.
dont: Do not put the only way to do something in a toast.
Do not use toasts for errors inside forms. Show them next to the field.
accessibility: Radix Toast region with a label. Danger toasts are announced assertively.
Each tone has an icon and a colored edge, never color alone.
components.example:
const toast = useToast();
toast.show({ title: "Money sent", description: "Deniz gets ₺250,00 in a few seconds.", tone: "success" });

components.name: Tooltip
components.purpose: Extra information on hover and focus. Wrap the app in TooltipProvider.

props.name: content
props.description: Extra information only. Never put required information or actions in a tooltip.

props.name: children
props.description: A single focusable element.

do: Keep it to one short sentence.
dont: Do not put required information, fees or actions in a tooltip.
Do not wrap non-focusable elements.
accessibility: Shows on keyboard focus, hides on Escape. Content is linked to the trigger.
components.example: <Tooltip content="The fee is the same for every amount."><IconButton icon="info" label="About the fee" /></Tooltip>

components.name: AccountCard
components.purpose: Account summary with type, masked IBAN, balance and up to three quick actions.

props.name: name
props.description: For example "Everyday account".

props.name: type
props.description: For example "Current account" or "Savings".

props.name: actions
props.description: Up to three quick actions.

props.name: masked
props.description: Hide the balance digits.

props.name: footer
props.description: Extra content under the balance, for example an interest rate.

do: Give each action a text label. The first one is primary.
dont: Do not show the full IBAN on the card. Show it on the details screen.
Do not use icon-only quick actions.
accessibility: Article named by account name and type.
IBAN is masked visually and read as "IBAN ending in 1 3 2 6".
components.example: <AccountCard name="Everyday" type="Current account" iban={iban} balance={24580.35} currency="TRY" actions={[{ label: "Send", icon: "arrow-up-right", onClick: send }]} />

components.name: AmountDisplay
components.purpose: Money amount with locale formatting, tabular figures and a direction that never relies on color.

props.name: value
props.description: Positive number. Direction decides the sign. Negative values are treated as outgoing.

props.name: direction
props.description: incoming: plus sign and teal. outgoing: minus sign and ink, never red. neutral: no sign, for balances.

props.name: size
props.description: xl for the hero balance, lg for account cards, md and sm for lists.

props.name: pending
props.description: Not settled yet. Adds a clock icon and a "Pending" label.

props.name: masked
props.description: Replace digits with dots, for example when the user hides balances.

do: Use for every amount and balance.
Pass a positive `value` and set `direction`.
Use `pending` for money that has not settled.
dont: Do not color outgoing amounts red. Outgoing is ink with a minus sign.
Do not format amounts by hand.
Do not make fees smaller than the amount they belong to.
accessibility: Visual text is hidden. Screen readers hear "Money in: 1,250.00 Turkish lira".
Incoming uses a plus sign, outgoing a typographic minus (U+2212).
components.example: <AmountDisplay value={1250} currency="TRY" locale="tr-TR" direction="incoming" />

components.name: AmountInput
components.purpose: Money entry with the decimal keypad, locale formatting and a clear limit error.

props.name: value
props.description: Amount in major units (lira, not kuruş). null when empty.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum allowed, for example the available balance. Going over shows an error.

props.name: error
props.description: Overrides the built-in error.

do: Pass max as the available balance so the error explains the limit.
Show the available balance in hint.
dont: Do not use a plain TextField for money.
Do not block typing: show the error and let people fix it.
accessibility: inputMode="decimal" opens the number keypad. The error is linked to the field. Values use tabular figures.
components.example: <AmountInput label="Amount" currency="TRY" locale="tr-TR" max={24580.35} hint="Available: ₺24.580,35" />

components.name: BalanceHeader
components.purpose: Account balance with a hide and show control.

props.name: label
props.description: For example "Available balance".

props.name: hidden
props.description: Controlled hidden state.

props.name: meta
props.description: Supporting line, for example "Updated 2 minutes ago".

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions under the balance, usually Buttons with text labels.

do: Use once at the top of home or account screens.
Put Send and Request as text Buttons in `actions`.
dont: Do not hide the toggle. People check balances in public.
accessibility: Region named by the label. Toggle uses `aria-pressed` and changes its label.
Hidden balances read "Balance hidden".
components.example: <BalanceHeader label="Available balance" balance={24580.35} currency="TRY" locale="tr-TR" />

components.name: OTPInput
components.purpose: One-time code entry with paste, SMS autofill and clear errors.

props.name: onComplete
props.description: Called once when every digit is filled.

do: Say where the code was sent in `hint`.
Use `onComplete` to verify automatically.
dont: Do not split the code into separate inputs.
Do not clear the code on error. Let people fix one digit.
accessibility: One real input with `autocomplete="one-time-code"` and `inputMode="numeric"`.
Spaces and letters are stripped, so pasting "482 913" works.
components.example: <OTPInput label="Verification code" hint="We sent a code to •••• 4821" onComplete={verify} />

components.name: QuickActions
components.purpose: Row of shortcuts such as Send, Request, Top up and Pay bills.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the group, for example "Quick actions".

do: Keep to four actions on phones.
Use a badge only for a count that needs attention.
dont: Do not use icon-only shortcuts: every action has a text label.
accessibility: A labelled list of buttons or links. Each target is at least 44 px.
components.example: <QuickActions label="Quick actions" actions={[{ label: "Send", icon: "send", onClick: send }]} />

components.name: TransactionRow
components.purpose: One transaction: merchant, category, date, amount and status.

props.name: amount
props.description: Positive number. Direction decides the sign.

props.name: icon
props.description: One of the names in `icons` at the top of this manifest.

do: Use inside List or any `ul`.
Set `status` for pending and declined so a badge appears.
dont: Do not color the row by direction.
Do not build transaction rows from ListItem.
accessibility: The whole row reads as one sentence: merchant, category, date, direction, amount, status.
The sentence starts with the visible merchant name, so voice control works.
components.example: <TransactionRow merchant="Coffee Lab" category="Eating out" date={date} amount={85} direction="outgoing" currency="TRY" locale="tr-TR" icon="coffee" />
